What should have been done? The question with no answer stayed for a long time. Meeting other parents who had lost a child the same way, it became a little easier to breathe.
For a long time came the self-blame of having been right there and not noticing. At a group for people who had been through the same loss, it could finally be said out loud.
Long after the funeral the question 'why' remained. It took time to accept that it was no one's fault.
Days of playing together as children kept coming back. The family left behind agreed not to blame one another.
The family spoke of it gently and held one another up.
